questions.q: [KAUST Thuwal Finals] Let \( \zeta = e^{2\pi i / 5} \) be a primitive \( 5 \)-th root of unity (plotted on the Argand diagram). Evaluate the exact complex product \[ \prod_{k=1}^{4} \left(2 - \zeta^k\right). \]
questions.answer: Because \( 1, \zeta, \zeta^2, \dots, \zeta^{4} \) are all \( 5 \) roots of \( z^{5} - 1 \), dividing out \( (z - 1) \) yields the cyclotomic identity \[ \prod_{k=1}^{4} (z - \zeta^k) = \frac{z^{5} - 1}{z - 1} = 1 + z + \dots + z^{4}. \] Substituting \( z = 2 \) gives \( 31 \).

questions.q: [KAUST Academy] Applying the Roots-of-Unity Filter with \( \omega = e^{2\pi i / 3} \) (shown on the unit circle), compute the exact stepped binomial sum \[ \sum_{\substack{0 \le j \le 6 \\ j \equiv 0 \pmod 3}} \binom{6}{j}. \]
questions.answer: Let \( P(x) = (1 + x)^{6} \). By the Roots-of-Unity Filter, \[ \sum_{j \equiv 0 \pmod 3} \binom{6}{j} = \frac{1}{3}\left(P(1) + \omega^{-0}P(\omega) + \omega^{-0}P(\omega^2)\right). \] Using \( 1 + \omega = -\omega^2 \) and \( 1 + \omega^2 = -\omega \), the sum simplifies to \( \frac{1}{3}\left(2^{6} + 2\cos\frac{(6 - 0)\pi}{3}\right) = 22 \).

questions.q: [KAUST Academy — Cambridge Summer Prep] Find the coefficient of \( x^{10} \) in the formal power series expansion of \[ G(x) = \frac{1}{(1 - x^{1})(1 - x^{2})(1 - x^{5})}, \] i.e., the number of non-negative integer solutions \( (u, v, w) \) to \( 1u + 2v + 5w = 10 \).
questions.answer: Expanding each geometric factor \( (1 - x^d)^{-1} = \sum_{k \ge 0} x^{kd} \), \( [x^{10}]G(x) \) counts non-negative triples \( (u, v, w) \) with \( 1u + 2v + 5w = 10 \). Case-splitting on \( w = 0, 1, \dots, \lfloor 10/5 \rfloor \) and summing \( \#\{(u,v): 1u + 2v = 10 - 5w\} \) yields exactly \( 10 \).
